measures.unit_basis: $/unit (one 90 kBtu/h / 7.5-ton air-cooled commercial packaged rooftop unit)

like_for_like.basis: Code-minimum in-kind replacement: air-cooled small commercial packaged rooftop air conditioner, 90 kBtu/h (7.5 tons), same size class as the heat pump (the RTU the owner would install anyway at end of life)
like_for_like.note: EIA (2023), 'Updated Buildings Sector Appliance and Equipment Costs and Efficiency' (base 2022$), Appendix A, 'Commercial Rooftop Air Conditioners' DATA table, p.135, 90 kBtu/h (7.5 tons). Total Installed Cost (2022$), 2022 columns: low=$11,870 (Current Standard, i.e. code-minimum), base=$11,870 (Typical - identical to Current Standard in the 2022 column), high=$17,600 (High-efficiency). Verbatim; not interpolated. Incremental (capex - like_for_like) = 1,030 / 3,070 / 1,260 per unit at low/base/high - non-negative at every point.

measures.notes: CORRECTED (soapbox-costing issue #4). One unit = one 90 kBtu/h (7.5-ton) air-cooled commercial packaged rooftop unit. capex from EIA (2023), 'Updated Buildings Sector Appliance and Equipment Costs and Efficiency' (base 2022$), Appendix A, 'Commercial Rooftop Heat Pumps' DATA table, p.139, Total Installed Cost (2022$), 2022 columns: low=$12,900 (Current Standard), base=$14,940 (Typical), high=$18,860 (High-efficiency). All figures verbatim from the source tables (no interpolation). PRIOR VALUES ($4,000/4,990/5,980) WERE WRONG: they are the EIA RESIDENTIAL Central Air Conditioner, 36 kBtu/h (3-ton) table (Appendix A, p.27) - low/high were that table's 2015 Installed Base ($4,000) and 2022 High ($5,980) endpoints and base ($4,990) was their midpoint (interpolated). Correction raises per-unit scale ~3x (base $4,990 -> $14,940) because one unit is now a 7.5-ton commercial RTU, not a 3-ton residential split system. like_for_like is a code-minimum in-kind 7.5-ton packaged rooftop AC (same report, p.135) so the incremental captures only the heat-pump premium. cost_breakdown (0.5/0.4/0.1) and contingency_pct (0.15) are unchanged from the prior seed and are NOT independently sourced from EIA (EIA reports only a single Total Installed Cost). Escalation base_year kept at 2022 (EIA base year).

ACEEE Summer Study 2016 paper 3-345: VRF ~$18/ft2 vs code-min baseline $12-15/ft2 (PRIMARY-DOC/summary). low/high derived as a +/-3 spread around the reported $18/ft2 anchor (no explicit VRF-specific range in source) -- tuned-base band, flag for tightening against a real VRF-specific range.

SECONDARY sanity-band only (GeothermalFinder/EnergySage 2025-26 guides), office tier $4,500-7,500/ton (loop drilling = 50-70% of vertical closed-loop cost). EIA (2022$) and ORNL GeoVision (2019, ORNL/TM-2019/502) carry authoritative commercial GSHP figures, but a specific $/ton was not extracted from those PDFs in this pass -- flagged for ingest. source: tuned-base.

EIA 2023 study, base 2022$, centrifugal/screw/scroll chillers, $440-1390/ton total installed across capacity/efficiency tiers, PRIMARY-EXTRACTED. Underlying per-unit values are derived from proprietary RSMeans 2023 + Guidehouse; citing only EIA's published aggregation (public domain).

like_for_like.basis: ASHRAE 90.1-2019 minimum-efficiency code-compliant centrifugal chiller (like-for-like baseline replacement)
like_for_like.note: EIA 2023 study (Appendix A, Commercial Centrifugal Chillers - Water-Cooled, p.126), 2022$: ASHRAE 90.1-2019 baseline installed cost is $480/ton (400-ton) to $540/ton (600-ton) — base=510 uses that midpoint directly. low/high (350/620) are widened around it (not independently sourced) so the incremental this entry's capex.low/high (440/1390, a wider size/technology mix than the 400-600 ton centrifugal table this figure is drawn from) never goes negative. Incremental at base = 915 - 510 = 405/ton.

measures.notes: SECONDARY trade sanity band (Oxmaint 2026), mid-size commercial condensing boiler (1-3 MMBtu) installed cost. EIA carries an authoritative per-unit boiler figure in its Appendix A ('Commercial Gas-Fired Boilers'), but the specific $/unit was not extracted in this pass -- flagged for ingest. source: tuned-base.

like_for_like.basis: standard non-condensing commercial gas boiler (code-minimum replacement)
like_for_like.note: Oxmaint 2026 reports a condensing upgrade premium of ~$6-10K/unit over a standard replacement; like-for-like = condensing base - that premium, so incremental (premium only) = ~$6/8/10K per unit. Apply the incremental as the CapEx basis ONLY when the existing boiler is at/near end-of-life (per the asset's Audette RUL); for a healthy boiler the full capex is incremental.

measures.notes: PNNL-21944 (Oct 2012, DOE Contract DE-AC05-76RL01830), office-building scenario: maximum installed controller cost per packaged unit yielding a 3-yr payback, $1,560-2,990/RTU, PRIMARY-EXTRACTED. These are 'max acceptable for 3-yr payback' figures, not mean market bid prices -- treat as an upper-bound-anchored band; retail-building tier ($4,180-8,390/RTU) was not seeded separately.

LBNL (Mills, Building Commissioning: A Golden Opportunity, 2009), existing-buildings RCx: median ~$0.30/ft2, range $0.05-0.40/ft2, PRIMARY-DOC/summary, 2009$. ~16% energy savings, payback ~1.1yr reported alongside.

LBNL Mills & Sartor, Energy Use and Savings Potential for Laboratory Fume Hoods (OSTI 862161, 2006): CAV->VAV retrofit ~$6,000/hood, mid-2000s $, PRIMARY-DOC/summary; retrofit kits reported at 10-20% of a new hood's cost. low/high derived as a +/-20% band around the reported $6,000 anchor (source gives a single point figure) -- tuned-base band.

DOE Building America, Cost Analysis of Roof-Only Air Sealing and Insulation Strategies: roof air-seal+insulation to R-20 ~$10.25-20/ft2 roof area, PRIMARY-DOC/summary. Source scope is RESIDENTIAL; applied here as a commercial tuned-base proxy pending a commercial-specific envelope survey. Base year is not explicitly stated in the source; a conservative 2015 Building America-era vintage is assumed pending verification -- flag.

SECONDARY trade guide (HireElectrical / National Efficiency Supply 2026), commercial LED retrofit $0.50-5.00/ft2. No authoritative redistributable commercial LED $/ft2 survey was found in this research pass (DOE SSL/CALiPER, GSA Green Proving Ground, and utility TRMs are flagged for future ingest). source: tuned-base.

SECONDARY trade guide (eilitetech), example 75HP VFD install $12k-18k implies ~$160-240/HP. The $80-250/HP figure elsewhere in the source is a utility prescriptive REBATE, not an install cost, and was deliberately excluded. No authoritative installed-cost survey was found; DOE UMP Ch.18 is an M&V protocol, not a cost source. source: tuned-base.

CED Engineering, HVAC -- Guide to Demand Control Ventilation (course monograph, PRIMARY-DOC/summary): DCV adds ~$1-3/cfm of outside air; CO2 sensors now <$200 (was >$500 a decade ago). Base year not stated in source; conservatively dated 2015 pending verification -- flag. ERV/HRV per-unit costs ($4k-20k+/unit, SECONDARY sanity band only, no clean $/cfm survey) were not seeded separately; utility TRMs (IL, CA DEER, NY) are the recommended authoritative substitute per the research doc.

EIA 2023 study (Appendix A, Commercial Heat Pump Water Heaters, p.155), 2022$, single typical unit (50kW / 171 kBtu/h output, COPh 3.9). EIA reports this as a single point, not a range: the commercial HPWH market is extremely small (ENERGY STAR lists only ~2 manufacturers), so no low/high efficiency-tier spread exists the way most other equipment categories in this file have. PRIMARY-EXTRACTED.

like_for_like.basis: Conventional commercial gas-fired storage water heater, ~100gal/199kBtu/h (comparable service scale), current-standard efficiency, replacement-market cost
like_for_like.note: EIA 2023 study (Appendix A, Commercial Gas-Fired Storage Water Heaters, p.149), 2022$, current-standard unit, replacement-market cost ($5,140) — EIA's own range runs $5,140 (replacement market) to $8,410 (new construction); replacement-market is the relevant comparator for a like-for-like fuel-switch at an existing building. Incremental (heat pump premium over a like-for-like gas replacement) = $59,940 - $5,140 = $54,800.

measures.notes: NESCAUM (2023), 'Heat Pump Water Heaters in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic - Costs and Market Trends', Table 18 (p.35), 2023$: 240V in-unit HPWH (45-55 gal) TOTAL INSTALLED cost, no panel upgrade = $3,152 avg (state range $2,756 VA - $3,904 NY); WITH panel upgrade = $5,427 avg (up to $7,533 NY). capex.low/base use the no-panel-upgrade case; capex.high uses the with-panel-upgrade average because in-unit multifamily electrification frequently triggers an electrical panel upgrade. PRIMARY-EXTRACTED; regional (NE/Mid-Atlantic) figure applied nationally -> medium confidence. Corroborating: DNV/CPUC 2017 (CA MF HPWH installed ~$1,500-1,800) and CalNEXT 2025 (unitary 240V HPWH equipment ~$2,098). cost_breakdown material/labour split (~0.58/0.42) follows NESCAUM's equipment ($1,837) vs labour ($1,314) rows; the 0.05 equipment share is an allocation-judgment placeholder consistent with the rest of this file. NOTE: the task-suggested baseline source neea-pricing-water-heaters-2022 is a willingness-to-pay conjoint survey, NOT a measured cost, so the baseline was taken from NESCAUM's same-study electric-storage row instead.

like_for_like.basis: standard electric-resistance storage water heater (UEF 0.92, 40-50 gal) - code-minimum in-kind replacement
like_for_like.note: NESCAUM (2023) Table 17 (p.34), 2023$: electric-resistance storage water heater (UEF 0.92, 40-50 gal) TOTAL INSTALLED = $882 avg (state range $788 VA - $1,056 NY). Same study and base year as the HPWH figure -> clean like-for-like. Incremental (HPWH premium over a standard electric-storage replacement) at base year = $3,152 - $882 = $2,270/unit. Apply the incremental as the CapEx basis ONLY when the existing water heater is at/near end-of-life (per the asset RUL); for a healthy unit the full capex is incremental.

measures.notes: EIA 'Updated Buildings Sector Appliance and Equipment Costs and Efficiency' (2023, base 2022$), Residential Air-Source Heat Pumps table (full report p.39): ducted 3-ton (36 kBtu/h) split ASHP TOTAL INSTALLED cost - Current Standard SEER 14.0 = $6,730 (capex.low); ENERGY STAR V6.1 SEER 16.0 / Cold-Climate = $6,940 (capex.base); High-efficiency SEER 22.6 = $8,620 (capex.high). PRIMARY-EXTRACTED. SCOPE CAVEAT: EIA prices the WHOLE split system (ASHP figures are 'blower-coil' systems), not a condenser/outdoor-unit in isolation; EIA does not break out a condenser-only $/unit, so this $/unit is whole-split-system. Ductless mini-split (1-ton, $2,030 flat) is a different size class and is deliberately NOT used here.

like_for_like.basis: standard-SEER residential split-system central air conditioner (3-ton, coil-only) - code-minimum in-kind replacement
like_for_like.note: EIA (2023, 2022$), Residential Central Air Conditioners tables (full report p.27 North, p.28 South): standard-efficiency 3-ton coil-only split AC TOTAL INSTALLED cost - Current Standard SEER 13.0 (North) = $5,250; Current Standard SEER 14.0 (South) = $5,310; Typical SEER 14.6 (South) = $5,390. Same study and base year as the ASHP figure. SCOPE CAVEAT: the AC table is 'coil-only' (no blower) whereas the ASHP measure is 'blower-coil', so the incremental (~$1,480-3,230/unit) slightly overstates the pure equipment premium by roughly the cost of a blower. Incremental at base = $6,940 - $5,310 = $1,630/unit. Apply the incremental as the CapEx basis ONLY when the existing AC is at/near end-of-life.

measures.notes: Illinois Statewide Technical Reference Manual v13.0, Volume 3: Residential Measures, Section 5.7.4 'Heat Pump Swimming Pool Heater' (p.516), measure RS-MSC-HPPH-V01-230101. DEEMED single-value gross INSTALLED cost = $7,074/unit (includes material cost of heat pump, installation infrastructure, and labour); the TRM publishes no low/base/high band, so capex low=base=high. Underlying cost basis is the 2021 California TRM / SCE 'SWRE005-01 Cost Analysis.xlsm' (footnote 1872) -> base_year stamped 2021 (not pre-escalated; tool escalates at query time). AUTHORITATIVE (state regulatory deemed-cost manual). Deemed single point on a ~2021 basis -> medium confidence. cost_breakdown shares are allocation-judgment placeholders consistent with the rest of this file (the TRM does not decompose the cost). APPLICABILITY: the like_for_like baseline here is a GAS pool heater (per the IL TRM's gas-vs-heat-pump framing). For an all-electric property whose existing heater is electric-resistance, this gas baseline does not apply — the in-kind replacement is a standard electric-resistance heater, which needs its own sourced cost before the like_for_like credit is used on such an asset.

like_for_like.basis: standard gas-fired swimming-pool heater - code-minimum in-kind replacement
like_for_like.note: Same IL TRM section 5.7.4 table (p.516): gas-heater baseline gross installed = $5,158/unit. The TRM's own published incremental (heat pump over gas) = $1,916/unit, which equals $7,074 - $5,158 exactly. Apply the incremental as the CapEx basis ONLY when the existing gas pool heater is at/near end-of-life; otherwise the full $7,074 is incremental.

measures.unit_basis: $/unit (one standard-size self-priming residential in-ground pool filter pump)

like_for_like.basis: Low-efficiency single-speed pool filter pump (DOE efficiency level 0 / baseline) - the pre-standard single-speed pump replaced in kind
like_for_like.note: DOE DPPP Direct Final Rule, Table V-2 (p.231, 2015$), Standard-Size Self-Priming Pool Filter Pump: Baseline (EL0) gross Installed Cost = $481/unit. Verbatim, not interpolated. Incremental (variable-speed EL7 $853 - single-speed baseline EL0 $481) = $372/unit (2015$). APPLICABILITY: the adopted federal standard (recommended TSL3 = EL6, compliance 2021) effectively requires variable-speed for this pump class, so a new single-speed install is no longer code-legal - the $481 single-speed credit applies ONLY when an EXISTING single-speed pump is being replaced at end of life (end-of-life in-kind logic per the schema's like_for_like semantics).

measures.notes: GROSS installed cost sourced from U.S. DOE, 'Energy Conservation Standards for Dedicated-Purpose Pool Pumps' Direct Final Rule / TSD (docket EERE-2015-BT-STD-0008, Dec 2016), Table V-2 'Average LCC and PBP Results for Standard-Size Self-Priming Pool Filter Pump' (p.231), costs in 2015$. capex = variable-speed pump gross Installed Cost = $853/unit (EL7, variable-speed high hydro efficiency; EL6 variable-speed low hydro efficiency is also $853). like_for_like = single-speed baseline (EL0) gross Installed Cost = $481/unit. Efficiency-level definitions from Table IV-29 (p.182). These are Monte-Carlo national-average installed costs; DOE Table V-2 publishes a single average per efficiency level, not a low/base/high band, so capex and like_for_like are single points (low=base=high) - NOT interpolated. base_year stamped 2015 (2015$; the tool escalates at query time). CROSS-CHECK: IL TRM v13 §5.7.1 (p.505) publishes a variable-speed incremental of $314/unit in-ground over a TWO-SPEED federal-standard baseline; the DOE $372/unit incremental here is measured over a LOW-EFFICIENCY SINGLE-SPEED baseline (EL0). The two roughly reconcile and differ in the expected direction: a two-speed baseline (DOE EL5 = $823) is costlier than the single-speed EL0, leaving a smaller remaining increment to VSD, consistent with IL TRM's $314 < DOE's $372. confidence=medium (single national-average point, 2015$ vintage). cost_breakdown shares and contingency_pct (0.2) are allocation-judgment placeholders consistent with the pool-heat-pump-heater entry; DOE does not decompose the installed cost.
